name: Impossible-travel / geo-velocity for identity & account-takeover
category: New — flagship demo for beava's distance primitive
parent_research_topic: Beava use cases — current and potential applications of beava as a real-time feature server

domain_fit.domain_name: Impossible-travel / geo-velocity detection for identity and account-takeover
domain_fit.one_line_definition: An identity provider, fintech, or SaaS auth gate decides in <50 ms at sign-in (or step-up) whether the implied travel speed between the last successful authentication's geolocation and the current attempt's geolocation exceeds a physically plausible threshold (typically 500–1000 km/h, the cruise speed of a commercial airliner), and if so escalates to MFA / step-up / block.
domain_fit.representative_jobs_to_be_done: 1) Block ATO attempts at login when stolen credentials are replayed from a geographically inconsistent location (the canonical example: same account just logged in from New Jersey 22 minutes ago and is now logging in from Vietnam — a near-certain ATO signal). 2) Trigger adaptive MFA / step-up authentication on borderline impossible-travel events (high geo-velocity but plausible if the user is on a long-haul flight + airline Wi-Fi). 3) Feed an aggregated identity risk score (alongside device fingerprint, IP reputation, behavioural biometrics) that a Conditional Access / risk engine consumes to allow, challenge, or deny. 4) Provide a SOC / fraud-ops alert when a user account exhibits cross-continent travel velocity, with the historical trail for investigators. 5) Catch session-token theft or cookie-replay attacks where the stolen session is replayed from an attacker's geography.
domain_fit.event_shapes: Wire events typically: login_success {ts, account_id_hash, ip, lat, lon, country, city, asn, device_fp, ua_hash, mfa_used, auth_method}, login_attempt {ts, account_id_hash, ip, lat, lon, asn, device_fp, success, reason}, session_resume {ts, account_id_hash, ip, lat, lon, session_id, device_fp}, sensitive_action {ts, account_id_hash, ip, lat, lon, action_type} (e.g. password change, beneficiary add, fund transfer — PSD3 broadens SCA to these). The (lat, lon) pair comes from IP geolocation enrichment (MaxMind GeoIP2, IPinfo, ipregistry) performed by the auth gate before the event is pushed to beava, or — for mobile / device-SDK paths — from the device's own GPS / Wi-Fi-triangulated location.
domain_fit.feature_shapes: Maps almost one-to-one to beava's geo primitives in `python/beava/_agg.py`: `geo_velocity(lat='lat', lon='lon')` — lifetime max km/h between consecutive login events for an account_id_hash (the direct impossible-travel signal); `distance_from_home(lat='lat', lon='lon', samples=100)` — distance from current login to centroid of last N successful logins (the 'first time you've logged in from this region' signal, which Microsoft Entra calls 'unfamiliar sign-in properties'); `geo_distance(...)` — cumulative path length per account_id_hash over a window (long-haul travel pattern); `geo_spread(...)` — RMS dispersion around running centroid (does this account normally log in from 1 city, 3 cities, or 30?); plus complementary counters: `count(login_success, 1h/24h)`, `n_unique(country, 24h/7d)` per account, `n_unique(account_id, 1h)` per source-IP (the credential-stuffing cross-signal). Typically computed on a 1h / 24h / 7d / 30d sliding window per account, plus lifetime tracking for geo_velocity / distance_from_home.
domain_fit.entity_grain: Primary key is account_id_hash (the user). Secondary grains: device_fingerprint (cross-account impossible-travel on the same device implies device theft or stolen session), session_id (for token-replay detection), and (account_id_hash x device_fingerprint) pair. IP and ASN are dimensions, not entity keys here — they are inputs to the geo enrichment.
domain_fit.window_semantics_required: Lifetime + sliding. The core geo_velocity / distance_from_home primitives are inherently 'consecutive events' (state-of-the-last-point) and lifetime — they do not need a window. Complementary features (n_unique countries in 24h, count of cross-country logins in 7d) use sliding windows. Exact computation is the right choice — cardinality per account is low (each user has 1 'current geo'), so HLL / CMS sketches are not needed. Distance computation uses the Haversine formula, which is what beava's `geo_distance` and `geo_velocity` ops already implement (`agg_geo.rs`).
domain_fit.exactly_once_or_idempotency_needs: At-least-once is acceptable. A duplicated login event biases the geo_velocity feature in the safe direction (it makes the feature look slightly more anomalous, not less). Decisions are risk scores, not money — there is no double-spend equivalent. Idempotency by (account_id, session_id, ts) is a nice-to-have for clean dashboards but not required for correctness.

technical_fit.latency_budget: Read p99 <10 ms is the operational target for inline sign-in gating; <50 ms end-to-end before the login UX visibly degrades. The geo_velocity read is one of 20–100 features pulled inside the auth flow, so the per-feature budget is tight. beava's sub-ms TCP+msgpack batch_get fits with headroom; the dominant external latency is the IP-geolocation lookup (sub-ms with a local MaxMind GeoLite2 database, 10–100 ms via remote API).
technical_fit.feature_freshness_sla: Sub-second to single-digit-seconds end-to-end. The point of impossible-travel is to fire on the *current* login attempt against the *immediately preceding* successful login, so the previous-login state must already be in beava when the next request arrives. beava's push-on-event model with no broker hop comfortably hits this — the auth gate writes login_success and beava's geo state updates atomically before the next attempt arrives milliseconds later.
technical_fit.throughput_profile: Auth0 publicly reports >10 billion authentications per month (~3.8k EPS average; ~330M/day) across its multi-tenant fleet; individual large tenants see ~100M logins/day. Okta hosts hundreds of millions of web requests per day. Per-tenant peak EPS is typically 10–100x average due to traffic patterns + credential-stuffing waves. A single beava node at the published ~684k EPS sustained on an Apple-M4 core (TCP+msgpack, parallel=16) is far above what any single IDP tenant requires for the impossible-travel feature in isolation, and is comfortable even at the per-region shard of a global IDP. The geo features are computed once per login_success (not per request), which keeps the write volume bounded to authentication events — orders of magnitude below the per-request traffic a WAF sees. [uncertain] published EPS for Castle / Sift / Fingerprint ATO scoring tiers.
technical_fit.read_to_write_ratio: Roughly 1:1 to 2:1. Every login_success is one write (atomic update of geo_velocity / distance_from_home / geo_spread state for account_id_hash) and one or more reads of the prior state to feed the risk score. Sensitive non-login actions (password change, beneficiary add) generate additional reads against the same account_id_hash without updating the geo state.
technical_fit.state_size_estimate: Per-account state is tiny — a few floats for `geo_velocity` (last lat, last lon, last ts, running max km/h), a circular buffer of last N points for `distance_from_home(samples=N)` (e.g. N=100 ⇒ ~1.6 KB at 16 B/point), plus a centroid + RMS for `geo_spread`. At 2 KB / account, a SaaS app with 10M MAU is ~20 GB; a global IDP with 1B end-users would push toward 2 TB — beyond a single beava box's in-memory ceiling but tractable per-region or per-tenant. Time-to-live can purge dormant accounts aggressively (no need to keep geo state for users who haven't logged in in 90+ days).
technical_fit.cardinality_pattern: Slowly-growing on account_id_hash (the natural rate of net new users at the buyer). Bounded per account — each account has exactly one current 'last login geo'. This is one of the cleanest cardinality profiles for beava: no explosive IP/fingerprint blowup, no HLL/CMS sketches needed.
technical_fit.typical_state_lifecycle_and_ttl: 30–180 days per account is the common operational TTL — long enough to learn a user's travel pattern and detect 'unfamiliar sign-in', short enough to evict dormant users and respect GDPR data-minimisation. Lifetime tracking (Okta's 'Velocity behaviour' is effectively lifetime max) is the simplest implementation; a 30-day sliding equivalent reduces false positives from years-old reference points.
technical_fit.typical_feature_count_per_decision: Impossible-travel itself contributes ~3–6 features per login (geo_velocity, distance_from_home, geo_spread, n_unique_countries_24h, distance_from_last_login_km, time_since_last_login_s). At the full identity-risk decision, it is one slice of a 20–100+ feature batch_get that also pulls device-fp velocity, IP-failure-ratio, behavioural-biometric scores, etc. Strongly favours beava's batch_get path.
technical_fit.durability_requirements: Best-effort to crash-safe. If beava loses the last few minutes of geo state during a crash, the immediate downside is a brief window where impossible-travel cannot fire on the *very next* login (the prior point is missing) — degraded detection, not financial loss. beava's WAL + periodic snapshot is more than sufficient. For PSD3-regulated PSPs the broader fraud-monitoring system must be auditable, but beava's specific role as the hot-path geo aggregator does not need regulator-grade durability if a downstream sink persists the login events.
technical_fit.deployment_topology_fit: Excellent fit for single-binary, sidecar-to-auth-service, or regional deployments — the same topology where Castle, Fingerprint, and WorkOS Radar already sit. beava as a sidecar next to the IDP's authentication service (or embedded in WAF/edge logic) maps directly. The hard limit is multi-region active-active for a global IDP: beava v0 has no cross-region replication, so a user logging in from EU then APAC within 30s would hit two separate beava shards and the impossible-travel signal would be lost across the partition. Buyers solve this either with regional pinning (route all of an account's auth events to the same beava shard via account_id_hash mod N) or with an external coordination layer.

commercial_fit.who_buys: Identity-platform engineering and platform-security teams at: (a) workforce & customer identity providers (Okta, Auth0, Microsoft Entra, Ping, ForgeRock, WorkOS, Stytch, Clerk, Frontegg, Descope, FusionAuth, SuperTokens), (b) fintech / neobank ATO teams (Wise, Revolut, Chime, Nubank, Monzo, N26, Cash App), (c) ATO-defence and behavioural-integrity vendors (Castle, Fingerprint, Sift, SEON, Sardine, Verisoul), (d) SecOps / detection-engineering teams at enterprises with Conditional Access stacks (the buyers of Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps' impossible-travel signal), and (e) consumer-platform trust & safety teams at marketplaces, dating apps, social networks where session takeover has high abuse impact. Distinctly NOT the corporate finance fraud team — this is platform / identity / SecOps.
commercial_fit.market_size_signal: Account-takeover is a major and growing market segment: U.S. ATO losses estimated at ~$17B in 2025 (up from ~$13B in 2023); 29% of U.S. adults (~77M people) experienced an ATO in 2024; credential-stuffing volume against consumer login endpoints grew 148% YoY through Q4 2025; average confirmed ATO incident costs ecommerce brands ~$12,000 in direct loss; 83% of organisations were hit by at least one ATO attack in the past year. The IAM market — within which impossible-travel sits as a built-in risk signal — is dominated by Okta ($2.6B FY2025 revenue, ~41% market share by some estimates) with Microsoft Entra, Ping, ForgeRock as the major incumbents; the broader fraud-detection-and-prevention market is projected to add ~$190B at 34.7% CAGR 2025–2030. Vendor-level price points: Castle starts at $200/mo for 100k requests; WorkOS Radar is sold as part of the WorkOS platform; Microsoft prices impossible-travel as part of Entra ID P2 + Defender for Cloud Apps (M365 E5 tier). [uncertain] specific ARR contribution of impossible-travel as a sub-feature within each platform.
commercial_fit.urgency_drivers: 1) PSD3 / PSR (provisional agreement Nov 2025; PSR likely in force Feb–Apr 2026; first SCA enforcement wave late 2026 to early 2027) explicitly broadens Strong Customer Authentication to login, mandate setup, beneficiary management, device recovery, and spending-limit changes, AND requires real-time behavioural and device monitoring as a fraud-prevention measure — impossible-travel is one of the cheapest, highest-signal features to satisfy this. 2) DORA (in force Jan 17, 2025) imposes operational-resilience requirements on EU financial firms' anti-fraud stacks. 3) ATO loss growth (148% YoY credential-stuffing volume, $17B annual losses) is forcing platform teams to add identity-risk features fast. 4) The Auth0 / Okta / Microsoft Entra reference implementations (Velocity behaviour, Sign-in risk, Impossible travel) have made impossible-travel a buyer-expected default — IDPs that lack it look behind the market. 5) AI-driven credential-stuffing toolkits and residential-proxy networks make impossible-travel one of the few signals that does NOT degrade when attackers humanise their behaviour (the attacker still has a physical location).
commercial_fit.regulatory_or_audit_constraints: PSD3 / PSR1 (EU payments — real-time behavioural monitoring as a mandatory fraud-prevention measure); DORA (operational resilience, Jan 2025); GDPR / CCPA (IP and geolocation are personal data — argues for short TTL, hashed account IDs, no raw IP retention; beava's in-memory + WAL + per-key TTL story aligns well, but lack of TLS / auth in v0 blocks regulated deployment); SOC 2 Type II (table stakes for enterprise IDP customers; lack of audit log and authN in beava v0 is a blocker); HIPAA only indirectly (when the IDP gates a healthcare app); PCI-DSS only when the auth gate fronts a payment flow (in which case 3DS / TRA exemption logic also lives nearby).
commercial_fit.time_to_value_signal: Fastest-to-demo use case in the entire beava use-case catalog. Because beava already ships `geo_velocity`, `geo_distance`, `geo_spread`, and `distance_from_home` as first-class primitives in `python/beava/_agg.py` (and the Rust implementation in `crates/beava-core/src/agg_geo.rs`), a working impossible-travel demo with synthetic events + a one-page Python `@bv.event` / `@bv.table` schema + a CLI that scores a stream of login events is realistically a 1-day build. A polished single-page web demo (map of the user's travel + km/h gauge + 'CHALLENGE / BLOCK / ALLOW' verdict) is 2–3 days. Production pilot at an IDP behind TLS / mTLS and proper IP-enrichment is 2–4 weeks once the v0 TLS/auth gaps are closed.

competition.incumbents: Generic stack: Redis (geospatial commands GEOADD / GEODIST, plus a Lua-scripted Haversine velocity check, is the overwhelming default — Redis publishes 'fraud detection brain' case studies for banks); Aerospike for high-cardinality variants; Flink / Materialize / RisingWave for buyers building this in SQL on top of Kafka (RisingWave has a public blog 'Real-Time Features for Account Takeover Detection' demonstrating this pattern); Tecton / Feast / Chalk / Hopsworks / Fennel as online feature stores feeding XGBoost-class ATO scorers. Datadog and Elastic ship 'detect impossible-travel' as a SIEM rule.
competition.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Built-in implementations inside identity platforms: Okta 'Velocity behaviour detection' (configurable 500 mph / 805 km/h threshold by default, ships in Identity Engine and Classic Engine), Microsoft Entra ID Protection 'Impossible travel' (P2-licensed, surfaced in Defender for Cloud Apps), Auth0 Adaptive MFA / Bot Detection, Ping Identity 'Impossible travel' fundamentals, WorkOS Radar (a dedicated WorkOS product line for ATO defence including impossible-travel), Stytch device-intelligence + impossible-travel signals; standalone ATO-defence vendors with their own impossible-travel signals: Castle (Account Takeover Score), Fingerprint (Velocity Signals product line), Sift (Account Takeover product), SEON (account-takeover risk assessment), Sardine, Verisoul (impossible-travel as a signal in its docs.verisoul.ai catalog), Memcyco, Feedzai, BioCatch. Most of these are end-to-end products, not feature backends — beava would more naturally sit *underneath* a Castle/Fingerprint/Sardine-style vendor, or inside an in-house IDP team's stack, than displace any of them.
competition.beava_differentiator: 1) The `geo_velocity` / `distance_from_home` / `geo_distance` / `geo_spread` primitives are first-class in beava and not in any general-purpose competitor's primitive list — Redis exposes GEOADD/GEODIST but velocity-between-consecutive-events is hand-rolled Lua + key conventions; Flink / Materialize need user-defined functions; Tecton / Feast typically push this to user-written Python or PySpark. This is the one place beava ships a production-shaped operator that nobody else has built-in. 2) Single binary, no Kafka + Flink + Redis cluster — fits the auth-service sidecar / edge / PoP topology IDPs are already moving toward. 3) Sub-ms TCP+msgpack batch_get fits the inline auth-time budget. 4) Apache-2.0 with no open-core — attractive to IDPs and ATO-defence vendors that want to embed it rather than rent. 5) Push-on-event ingest model matches how auth gates already produce events (HTTP webhook, mobile SDK direct push). 6) The geo state is bounded per account (low cardinality, small per-entity footprint), so the impossible-travel use case is one of the highest-confidence fits for beava's in-memory model.
competition.where_beava_loses_today: 1) No TLS, no auth on :8080 / :8081 / :8090 — disqualifying for any external-facing IDP / regulated-fintech deployment; today beava is in-VPC-only or behind an mTLS-terminating proxy. 2) No in-process sharding — a global IDP with 1B end-users cannot fit geo state on one box and would need external account-id-mod-N hand-sharding. 3) No cross-region replication — a user logging in from EU then APAC within 30s would hit two different beava shards and the impossible-travel signal would be lost without an external coordination layer. 4) No triggers — buyers want 'when this account's geo_velocity crosses 1000 km/h, fire MFA challenge or webhook' as a push-callback primitive; beava today requires the auth gate to poll. 5) No IP-geolocation enrichment built in — beava expects (lat, lon) pre-resolved on the event, which means the buyer needs to integrate MaxMind / IPinfo / ipregistry separately (this is conventional but worth documenting as a producer responsibility). 6) No native handling of VPN / corporate-proxy / mobile-carrier false-positive suppression — beava computes raw geo_velocity, but the production-grade detector needs IP-reputation enrichment and device-fingerprint co-signal (Microsoft reports 75% false-positive reduction once VPN suppression + failed-login exclusion are added) — that logic lives in the buyer's risk engine, not in beava. 7) No multi-tenancy — an ATO-defence vendor serving many customers needs per-tenant namespaces and quotas. 8) No SOC-analyst surface — 'show me all accounts with geo_velocity > 800 km/h in the last hour' is a scan, not a primary-key get.
competition.integration_surface: Producers: identity provider auth service emitting login_success / login_attempt (HTTP webhook or direct TCP push), WAF / reverse proxy (Cloudflare Worker, Fastly Compute, Envoy) emitting auth-related events, mobile SDK pushing GPS-grade location directly. beava's HTTP/JSON :8080 fits the IDP webhook path; TCP+msgpack :8081 fits the high-throughput sidecar path. An IP-geolocation enrichment step (MaxMind GeoIP2, IPinfo, ipregistry — sub-ms with a local database, 10–100 ms via remote API) is a mandatory upstream step the producer owns. Consumers: the IDP's adaptive-MFA / Conditional Access engine (Okta Adaptive MFA, Entra Conditional Access, custom in-house), an ML risk scorer (XGBoost / LightGBM consuming `geo_velocity`, `distance_from_home`, etc. as features), and SIEM (Datadog, Elastic, Splunk) for SOC alerting.
competition.scoring_engine_coupling: Both. Most production deployments run a deterministic rule layer (e.g. 'if geo_velocity > 1000 km/h AND device_fp is new AND IP is not on corp-VPN allowlist, force MFA') *and* an ML scorer that consumes the same beava geo features as one slice of the input vector. beava as a pure feature backend stays decoupled from both — this is its natural seam.

adoption_signals.examples_or_demos_in_repo: No dedicated impossible-travel / ATO demo identified in the repository as of the snapshot reviewed. [uncertain] However, the geo primitives are already implemented and tested: `python/beava/_agg.py` defines `geo_velocity`, `geo_distance`, `geo_spread`, `distance_from_home`; the Rust core ships `crates/beava-core/src/agg_geo.rs`, `crates/beava-core/benches/phase11_buffer_geo.rs`, and `crates/beava-core/tests/geo_field_idx_resolution.rs`; the Python test suite includes `python/tests/v0/test_geo.py`. The generic fraud demo at `python/beava/demos/fraud/` (schema.json + events.jsonl) is the closest existing artefact but does not specifically demonstrate impossible-travel. Building a dedicated `python/beava/demos/impossible_travel/` demo is the single highest-leverage README addition for this domain.
adoption_signals.adversarial_pressure_level: High. ATO is actively adversarial (credential-stuffing toolkits, residential-proxy pools, session-token theft, AI-shaped human behaviour). However, geographic location is one of the *more stable* signals — attackers can spoof user-agent, fingerprint, and behaviour, but the IP geolocation reflects the attacker's actual egress point (modulo VPN). The arms race shows up in (a) attackers buying residential proxies in the victim's country to evade impossible-travel (which moves the detection burden to device-fp + behavioural signals), and (b) the well-documented VPN / corporate-proxy false-positive problem, which is a continuous tuning effort rather than a cat-and-mouse rewrite.

risk_and_non_goals.non_goals: 1) IP-geolocation enrichment itself — beava does not ship a MaxMind / IPinfo database lookup; the producer must resolve (ip → lat, lon) before pushing the event. This is the conventional split (Castle, Fingerprint, WorkOS Radar all do the same) but should be documented. 2) Device fingerprinting / behavioural biometrics — beava aggregates the features, it does not generate them; the device_fp comes from a separate SDK (FingerprintJS, Castle SDK, in-house). 3) The risk-engine decision itself (allow / challenge / deny) — beava exposes the features, the rule engine or ML scorer makes the call. 4) Long historical lookback for analyst forensics (90-day login trail for a specific user) — that belongs in a warehouse / SIEM, not in beava's in-memory hot tier. 5) Cross-account graph queries ('all accounts that have logged in from this IP in the last hour') — beava is keyed by account, not by IP. 6) VPN / corporate-proxy / Tor exit-node enrichment — that is a separate enrichment service (Spur, IPQS, MaxMind anonymous-IP) the buyer integrates upstream. 7) Acting as the IDP itself — beava sits behind one.
risk_and_non_goals.open_engineering_gaps: Concrete features beava would need to ship to make this domain production-grade, roughly in priority order: 1) TLS termination + mTLS on :8081 / :8090 plus an auth model (token, mTLS, or both) on the admin / push surfaces — without this, no production IDP / fintech can deploy beava externally. 2) A turnkey impossible-travel example in `python/beava/demos/impossible_travel/` covering: synthetic login event generator with realistic geo trajectories, a `@bv.event LoginSuccess` + `@bv.table(key=account_id_hash)` schema using `bv.geo_velocity` + `bv.distance_from_home` + `bv.geo_spread`, a CLI replay that prints km/h + ALLOW/CHALLENGE/BLOCK per event, and a one-page README that an engineer can run on a laptop in <5 minutes. This single demo is probably the highest-leverage marketing artefact beava can ship for the entire identity / ATO market. 3) Triggers / push-callback when `geo_velocity` crosses a threshold — buyers want 'fire webhook when this account's km/h > T' as a primitive, not polled. 4) A short whitepaper / blog explaining the VPN / corporate-proxy / failed-login false-positive problem and the recommended buyer-side enrichment pattern (Spur / MaxMind anonymous-IP / Tor list) so customers don't show up confused about false positives. 5) Documented per-key TTL so dormant-user geo state can be evicted aggressively (90-day default would match GDPR data-minimisation defaults). 6) Cross-region replication or a documented account-id-mod-N sharding pattern so global IDPs with multi-region auth paths don't lose the signal at region boundaries. 7) Multi-tenancy / per-namespace ACL for ATO-defence vendors hosting many customers on shared beava infrastructure. 8) Hooks for (or a documented pattern for) device-fingerprint cross-correlation so 'logins from the same device_fp suppress the impossible-travel alert' is easy to express. 9) Audit log + SOC 2 / GDPR posture document so the IDP / fintech buyer can pass procurement. 10) A scan / top-K surface ('show top accounts by geo_velocity in last 1h') for the SOC analyst.
risk_and_non_goals.trigger_action_required: Yes, materially. Impossible-travel decisions are intrinsically event-driven: when a login event arrives and `geo_velocity` exceeds threshold, the right action is to *immediately* escalate to MFA / block the session — not to wait for the next risk-engine poll cycle. Today the auth gate must explicitly read the feature on every login attempt; a beava trigger that fires a webhook when (or only when) the threshold is crossed would remove an entire poll loop from the buyer's auth path and make beava feel more like an active detector than a passive feature backend. This is one of the cleanest motivating use cases for the triggers gap across the entire beava roadmap.
